items.title: Finiteness and continuity of the Galois action on the connected components of a quasi-compact base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over k with separable algebraic closure, assuming X quasi-compact and the connected components of X over the closure open, the lemma states that there are finitely many such components and that the Galois action on them is continuous, and it observes that both hypotheses hold when X is of finite type over k (statement lines 1283-1300). The proof of finiteness is immediate: open components cover, the space is quasi-compact, so only finitely many appear (proof lines 1303-1306). Continuity comes from the descent of quasi-compact opens: each connected component is a quasi-compact open of the base change, hence defined over a finite subextension, so its stabilizer contains an open subgroup, which for the discrete topology is exactly continuity (proof lines 1307-1309). The last paragraph verifies the finite type case through Noetherianness giving finitely many irreducible, hence connected, components (proof lines 1310-1318). The claim is H2: three short steps, with the descent of the quasi-compact opens as the only input requiring care.
